incident.detail: During E3a prompt-variant preparation, `git checkout -- ds/agents/carr.py` reverted an uncommitted v7/v8 resident-adapter version (route_observation_mode, initialize_route_observation/initialize_controlled_plan, execution_feedback_v8). The original bytes were not in git and were not recoverable byte-for-byte from session artifacts.

recovery.method: Reconstructed from session traces: exact method-line layout matches the frozen version (MechanismFlags:23, CarrResident:45, __init__:48, initialize_route_observation:96, initialize_controlled_plan:106, record_emitted_message:134, should_wake:148, decide:163, rule_fallback:187, commit_execution:193, snapshot:276, _route_observation:302, _carr_messages:330).
recovery.verification: tests/test_carr_pilot.py, test_carr_e1_v2.py, test_carr_interaction_v2.py, test_carr_routes.py: 39 passed; only the frozen-hash guard fails because bytes differ in two one-line docstrings whose exact wording is unrecoverable.
recovery.functional_equivalence: All mechanism/mock and E1 v2 tests pass; _build_parts no longer raises the route_observation_mode TypeError.

impact.completed_runs: E2 r7 audit and E3 lanes started before the revert are unaffected: their provenance recorded the original sha256 at run start.
impact.new_runs: Any new E2/E3/E3a run now uses the reconstructed file; audits must reference the reconstructed sha256.
impact.pending: A formal re-freeze of the resident-adapter hash is required before the frozen-hash guard can pass; this amendment documents the change basis and keeps both hashes.

claim_boundary: This is an engineering/provenance amendment, not a science change; no experimental numbers are altered.
